name: Erie Indemnity

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo of Erie Insurance Group (Erie Insurance Group logo.svg); the Erie Insurance mark is the brand Erie Indemnity operates under

description: Erie Indemnity does not sell insurance itself and owns none of the insurer. It is the attorney-in-fact (manager) for the Erie Insurance Exchange, a reciprocal insurer owned by its policyholders, and the Exchange is Indemnity's only customer. Indemnity sells, underwrites and issues the Exchange's policies and handles claims and investment management, and in return keeps a management fee of up to 25% of the premiums the Exchange writes ($13.0 billion in 2025). Indemnity pays the agents' commissions and the overhead out of that fee, keeping about $0.6 billion of profit on the policy-issuance work, and is repaid at cost for claims services. The Exchange takes the underwriting risk and the policyholders own its surplus.

gics.industry: Insurance Brokers (to be verified; may be Property & Casualty Insurance)
gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6411 (Insurance Agents, Brokers & Service). Erie Indemnity carries no underwriting risk: it does not own the insurer. It manages the policyholder-owned Erie Insurance Exchange for a fee, so the P&C insurer label misleads.

hq.note: Pennsylvania business corporation; address not extracted

employees.note: 6,667 full-time employees; about 50% provide claims and life-insurance management services exclusively for the Exchange, which reimburses their cost monthly (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Policy issuance and renewal services
businessLines.how: A fee set by Indemnity's board each year (capped at 25%; effective 24.41% of Exchange premiums for policy services in H1 2026) applied to all direct and affiliated assumed premiums the Exchange writes, so revenue moves with Exchange premium (rate increases plus policy growth). Agent commissions (56.7% of the fee in 2025, computed) and overhead come out of it.
businessLines.description: Sales, underwriting and issuing of policies for the Exchange, including paying independent agents' commissions.

operatingProfit.note: computed: $3,131.8M fee less $2,513.4M cost of operations (commissions $1,777.0M plus non-commission $736.4M)

businessLines.name: Administrative services
businessLines.how: A small extra fee (about 0.59% of Exchange premiums in H1 2026) plus a dollar-for-dollar reimbursement of what Indemnity spends on claims and life-insurance staff, so the reimbursement adds revenue and cost equally and no profit.
businessLines.description: Claims handling, life-insurance management and investment management for the Exchange.

revenue.note: management fee revenue; plus $836.6M of reimbursements for claims cost

businessLines.revenueNote: management fee revenue; plus $836.6M of reimbursements for claims cost

businessLines.name: Investment income (not a segment)
businessLines.how: Interest, dividends and gains on Indemnity's own portfolio; small next to the fee.
businessLines.description: Return on Indemnity's own fixed maturity and equity portfolio.

brands.name: Erie Insurance (the Exchange and its subsidiaries; customer, not owned)
brands.share: Sole customer; $13.0B direct and affiliated assumed premiums FY2025
